title: Msemen (Moroccan Layered Flatbread)
summary: A flour and semolina dough stretched paper-thin, folded with butter and semolina into squares and cooked on a griddle.
equipment: large flat griddle or frying pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Mix the flour, semolina, salt, sugar and yeast with the water and knead 6-8 min until very smooth and soft.

steps.title: Portion
steps.text: Mix the butter and oil, oil your hands and the worktop, divide the dough into 8 balls and rest them, oiled and covered, 15 min.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Spread one ball with oily hands into a very thin sheet; dot with fat and sprinkle with semolina, fold in the two sides to the middle, then fold the top and bottom to make a 10 cm square. Repeat with the rest.

steps.title: Flatten
steps.text: Rest the squares 10 min, then pat each out to about 15 cm.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on the griddle over medium heat 3-4 min each side until golden and crisp in spots.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Hot, with warm honey for dipping.

tips: Keep your hands and worktop well oiled.
Stretch as thin as you can; small holes are fine.
Cook over medium heat so the inside layers cook through.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature for 1 day or freeze; reheat in a dry pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
